vector_info.query_text: Can you help me understand Newton's third law?

intervention_mode_decision.primary_block: Surface confusion: the learner rejects equal forces because the effects are unequal. Hidden mistake: they are using damage or acceleration as the measure of force-pair size. Repair target: separate interaction force equality from unequal effects caused by different masses/structures. Probe reason: multi-select and sorting reveal whether the learner can keep force-pair size and outcome separate.

text_plan.instructional_goal: Select what can be true in a truck-bug collision.

expected_ideas: third-law forces are equal and opposite

misconception_markers.label: Effect treated as force size
misconception_markers.marker: Learner uses damage or acceleration to decide which force is bigger.

misconception_markers.label: Only the bigger object exerts force
misconception_markers.marker: Learner says the truck acts but bug does not push back.

presentation_support.text: Use partner dance practice and timing to reveal the structure, then immediately bridge back to formal physics.
First separate the hidden quantities, then use the probe to test the distinction.

prompt.full_prompt:
In partner dance, the contact push between two people is one shared interaction: each person feels the partner's push. But they may move differently if one is braced and the other is not.

For a truck and a bug, select all that can be true:
A. The truck pushes the bug and the bug pushes the truck with equal-size forces.
B. The bug can have a much larger acceleration/effect.
C. The bug has a smaller force because it is smaller.
D. Equal forces must cause equal damage.

Formal bridge-back: Newton's third-law pair is about force during the interaction; acceleration/effect also depends on mass and structure.
prompt.reshaping_explanation: Use partner dance: two dancers feel the same hand push, but their movement can differ depending on footing and body position. Bridge back to equal-and-opposite interaction forces versus unequal acceleration/effect.
prompt.root_problem_explanation: Surface confusion: the learner rejects equal forces because the effects are unequal. Hidden mistake: they are using damage or acceleration as the measure of force-pair size. Repair target: separate interaction force equality from unequal effects caused by different masses/structures. Probe reason: multi-select and sorting reveal whether the learner can keep force-pair size and outcome separate.
